subject.title: Feature: Activity-aware run timeout (wall-clock timeout kills active multi-tool runs)

question: Should OpenClaw keep `timeoutSeconds` as the hard wall-clock cap and add a separate idle/liveness timeout, or should `timeoutSeconds` itself become activity-aware?
rationale: Both shapes are technically plausible, but the choice changes core runtime semantics, config schema, resource ceilings, and how the existing partial timeout PRs should be reviewed.

options.title: Add idle plus hard cap
options.body: Introduce an explicit idle/liveness budget while keeping a hard maximum run ceiling so productive runs can continue without removing runaway protection.

options.title: Only improve timeout messaging
options.body: Keep wall-clock timeout semantics and land user-visible timeout notices or progress previews so users understand why long turns stopped.

options.title: Limit fixes to narrow slices
options.body: Treat subagent idle watchdogs, Telegram progress previews, and timeout notices as separate fixes while leaving the core run timeout contract unchanged for now.

recommendation.title: Add idle plus hard cap
recommendation.body: Introduce an explicit idle/liveness budget while keeping a hard maximum run ceiling so productive runs can continue without removing runaway protection.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner candidate has the strongest current-main history on the extracted timeout, gateway abort, maintenance, and idle-watchdog surfaces that the decision would touch.
